relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: In 1910, Poerbatjaraka moved to Batavia to take the Archaeology Service position.

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.role: assistant to a scholar of Javanese culture Dr. G. A. J. Hazeu
relations.evidence: After several years in Batavia, he was recruited by Leiden University in the Netherlands. He became assistant to a scholar of Javanese culture Dr. G. A. J. Hazeu, and taught Javanese language classes.

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: He completed his doctor's degree cum laude in 1926, with his thesis titled "Agastya in den Archipel" ("Agastya in Nusantara").

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.object: Museum of the Royal Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences
relations.evidence: He then returned to Batavia and worked at the Museum of the Royal Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences (today the National Museum of Indonesia), and catalogued the museum's large collection

relations.subject: H. J. de Graaf
relations.evidence: In Batavia, he also met the future historian of Java, H. J. de Graaf, to whom he gave weekly lessons in Javanese culture and language between 1927 and 1930. De Graaf later considered Poerbatjaraka his "revered teacher"

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: After Indonesia's independence, he became a professor, teaching at Gajah Mada University in Jogjakarta

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: teaching at Gajah Mada University in Jogjakarta, the University of Indonesia in Jakarta, and Udayana University in Denpasar, Bali.

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: teaching at Gajah Mada University in Jogjakarta, the University of Indonesia in Jakarta, and Udayana University in Denpasar, Bali.

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: He was one of the founders of Udayana's Literature Department.

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
relations.evidence: Among his notable works, he published studies on Agastya, the Old Javanese works Smaradahana, Arjunawiwaha, Ramayana and, with C. Hooykaas, the Bharatayudha.

relations.subject: Poerbatjaraka
